title: Large-Key Block Ciphers as Tweak Inputs
summary: The general use of a large block-cipher key as a tweak lacks clear security conditions; the half-key AES-256 approach is considered a very bad idea because of related-key attacks.

formal_statement.body: Determine whether, and under what security conditions, the key input of a block cipher whose key is large relative to its block size can generally be used to supply the tweak input when constructing a tweakable block cipher. A specific approach that allocates half of the AES-256 key input to the tweak is considered a very bad idea because of related-key attacks against AES-256.

scope.domain: Design and security analysis of tweakable block-cipher constructions using block ciphers with keys large relative to their block sizes.
parameters: Key size relative to block size — identifies the large-key setting
Tweak input — the input potentially supplied by the block-cipher key
Half of the AES-256 key input — the specific allocation discussed
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether the key input can generally serve as the tweak input, and the security conditions under which it can do so, remains unresolved.

citations.label: ZMAC: A Fast Tweakable Block Cipher Mode for Highly Secure Message Authentication

progress.summary: The source raises the issue while discussing block ciphers with keys large relative to their block sizes and says it remains unclear whether the key input can generally serve as a tweak input. It illustrates the concern with allocating half of AES-256's key input to the tweak, described as a very bad idea because of related-key attacks.
citation_labels: Tetsu Iwata et al., ZMAC: A Fast Tweakable Block Cipher Mode for Highly Secure Message Authentication
